sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul (dir.). SEAlang Mon-Khmer Languages Project, Bahnaric branch: 'Introduction' and 'Sources' pages. http://sealang.net/mk/bahnaric.htm (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No stress statement. Intro gives general Bahnaric typology (sesquisyllables, registers, vowel length) without mentioning stress. Sources page identifies the only primary Takua material: 'Maier, Jacqueline. 1964. English - Takua Vocabulary. Copy held by Summer Institute of Linguistics Library Bangkok, Takua folder 495.969.'

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2009. How many branches in a tree? Cua and East (North) Bahnaric. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 193-204. Pacific Linguistics 605. Canberra: ANU. (Glottolog ref 20943; whole volume open, CC BY-SA, ANU hdl:1885/146753)
sources.note: Nothing. Takua appears only in Thomas & Headley's 1970 list (p.194), in fn.3 p.195 ('The listing by Thomas of Takua alongside Cua is incongruous, since it is solidly North Bahnaric. Perhaps Thomas confused Takua with Kotua') and in the list of established North Bahnaric languages on the 1966 SIL map (p.196). The paper is about Cua/Kotua historical phonology (nasal hardening, registers); no word-structure or stress statement for Takua.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2002. Genetic classification of the Bahnaric languages: a comprehensive review. Mon-Khmer Studies 32:1-24.
sources.note: Nothing; classification review by historical phonology and lexicostatistics. scanned text contains no Takua data and no statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1973. Eastern North Bahnaric: Cua and Kotua. Mon-Khmer Studies 4:113-118.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Historical phonology (final nasal hardening, lack of register, r>zero, affricates) of Cua and 'Kotua' from a 200-word list taken at Mang Buk 1969. NB: this Kotua is Katua [kta] (Kontum/Quang Ngai border), not Takua; examined because Glottolog/multitree list 'Kotua' among Takua alt names and Sidwell 2009 flags the confusion.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2015. 'Bahnaric' (and 'Austroasiatic classification') in Mathias Jenny & Paul Sidwell (eds.), The Handbook of Austroasiatic Languages, vol. 1. Leiden: Brill.
